title: ip_restriction plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ip_restriction` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component IpRestrictionConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

IpRestrictionConfig.description: Plugin: ip_restriction — IP/CIDR allow/deny enforcement. Rules are validated and compiled at config load time into sorted, merged numeric intervals; invalid IPv4/IPv6 addresses or CIDR prefixes reject plugin creation. Request lookup is allocation-free, lock-free, and logarithmic in the number of non-overlapping intervals. The authoritative client IP is parsed/canonicalized once per request or stream session and reused by every plugin instance. IPv4 octets must use canonical unsigned decimal notation (for example, `010.1.2.3` and `+10.1.2.3` are rejected). Supports IPv4 exact and CIDR (`/0`-`/32`) and native IPv6 exact and CIDR (`/0`-`/128`). IPv4-mapped IPv6 rules normalize to IPv4, so mapped CIDRs accept only `/96`-`/128` (equivalent to IPv4 `/0`-`/32`); shorter mapped prefixes are rejected as ambiguous. CIDR prefixes must be canonical unsigned decimal (`/08`, `/+8`, and `/096` are rejected). IPv6 zone identifiers (e.g. `%eth0`) on rules or client IPs are stripped before matching; a rule's zone must be non-empty. Runs on every protocol — HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, TCP, UDP, and DTLS. HTTP-family requests are checked per request; TCP/TLS, UDP/DTLS, and WebSocket sessions are checked once at admission, and an established session is not re-evaluated when a reload changes the policy. Responses the gateway produces before this plugin runs — route 404/405, gRPC method admission, a `cors` preflight answer, `request_termination` — still reach a denied client. Every rejection records `ip_restriction.reason` (`unparseable_client_ip`, `not_in_allow_list`, or `ip_denied`) in transaction-log metadata. Config must be an object, unknown properties and null values are rejected, and at least one of `allow` or `deny` must be non-empty.

allow.description: Allowed IP addresses or CIDR ranges (IPv4 or IPv6). Empty list disables allow-list enforcement. Each entry must match `IpRestrictionRule`.

deny.description: Denied IP addresses or CIDR ranges (IPv4 or IPv6). Always takes precedence over an `allow` match. Each entry must match `IpRestrictionRule`.

IpRestrictionRule.description: One IP or CIDR rule admitted by `ip_restriction`. Surrounding whitespace follows Rust `str::trim` Unicode `White_Space` semantics. IPv4 octets must be canonical unsigned decimal (no leading zeros, no `+`), and CIDR prefixes must be canonical unsigned decimal too (`/8`, never `/08`, `/+8`, or `/008`). Native IPv6 follows the standard textual grammar, including `::` compression in front of an embedded dotted IPv4 tail (`2001:db8::1:192.0.2.1`). It may be bracketed and may carry a zone identifier, which must be non-empty and contain no whitespace, `/`, or `]`; CIDR prefixes sit outside the brackets. IPv4 CIDR prefixes are `/0`–`/32`; native IPv6 prefixes are `/0`–`/128`. IPv4-mapped IPv6 — any spelling whose value lies in `::ffff:0:0/96`, such as `::ffff:a.b.c.d`, `0::ffff:c000:201`, or `0:0:0:0:0:ffff::` — accepts exact addresses or CIDR `/96`–`/128` only.
